# Blaise 1.9.1: notes on Sonnet 5.5
The Claude subscription engine now writes your notes and memory digest with Sonnet 5.5.
## What changed
- **Sonnet 5.5 for the subscription engine.** In side-by-side tests on real meetings, 5.5 wrote more accurate notes and digests than 4.6 (fewer wrong names, dates and superseded decisions kept as if still decided) and finished in about half the time. The API engine stays on Sonnet 4.6. - **Room for long meetings.** The engine's output limit goes up to 32,000 tokens, so the digest of a two-hour meeting is no longer cut short. - **Your own commitments land in your action items.** A new notes prompt version, c6-v1.2, treats anything you say you will do yourself ("I'll…", "vou…") as your action item, even when you say it in passing. It is the new default for every engine; the earlier versions stay selectable. - **Upgrading from 1.9.0:** delivered in place by the updater. Meetings, transcripts, notes and settings untouched.
## Assets
- `Blaise-1.9.1.zip`: the notarised, stapled app (macOS 15.6.1+, Apple Silicon) - `blaise-meet-extension.zip`: the Chrome extension for Google Meet participant/speaker signals (unchanged)

# Blaise 1.9.0 — no more silent mic-only recordings
If macOS ever records your microphone but not the other side of the call, Blaise now tells you while the meeting is still going, instead of leaving you to find out afterwards. Contributed by Arthur Soares (@arthursoares) in #15.
## What changed
- **Missing call audio is visible.** An orange banner in the main window, a card in the menu-bar menu and one notification (no sound) per episode. Quiet calls are fine: silence still counts as audio arriving. - **Blaise tries to fix it.** Two automatic repairs, then a **Retry Call Audio** button and a shortcut to the audio permission settings. If a repair keeps failing while call audio is already missing, Blaise keeps recording your microphone instead of stopping. - **The meeting remembers.** Affected meetings are marked **Capture incomplete** in the library, and the note survives reprocessing, because audio that was never captured cannot come back. - **A start-of-recording bug is fixed.** A disk write failure in the first moments of a recording could leave it looking live while nothing was saved. It now stops and keeps what exists, like any other write failure. - **Upgrading from 1.8.0:** delivered in place by the updater. Meetings, transcripts, notes and settings untouched.
## Assets
- `Blaise-1.9.0.zip` — the notarised, stapled app (macOS 15.6.1+, Apple Silicon; fully tested on macOS 26 and 27) - `blaise-meet-extension.zip` — the Chrome extension for Google Meet participant/speaker signals (unchanged)

# Blaise 1.8.0 — the app now updates itself
From this version on, Blaise checks for a new release once a day and offers it in place: a dialog with the release notes, one click to install, and the app relaunches on the new build. There is also **Blaise → Check for Updates…** for whenever you want to look yourself.
## What changed
- **In-app updates via Sparkle 2.10.0.** Daily check, silent when there is nothing new. Nothing is ever downloaded or installed without your click; the "install automatically" option is deliberately not offered. - **Signed twice.** Every update is a notarised, Developer-ID-signed build, and the download itself carries an EdDSA signature that the app verifies against a key baked in at build time. A build without that key (a local `swift build`, a fork) never checks a feed. - **Known limit.** If a sheet is open in Blaise (say, the participant confirmation on a meeting) when you click "Install and Relaunch", macOS refuses the quit and nothing visible happens; the update installs the next time you quit Blaise. Close the sheet first, or just quit and reopen. - **Upgrading from 1.7.0:** this is the last version you download by hand. Same signing identity, no permission re-prompts; meetings, transcripts, notes and settings untouched.
## Assets
- `Blaise-1.8.0.zip` — the notarised, stapled app (macOS 15.6.1+, Apple Silicon; fully tested on macOS 26 and 27) - `blaise-meet-extension.zip` — the Chrome extension for Google Meet participant/speaker signals (unchanged)
